references.text: The context of the prohibition against following the crowd; warns against spreading false rumors and helping a wicked person as an unjust witness.
Command for fair judgment without favoring either the poor or the powerful, emphasizing impartial justice.
Prohibition against perverting justice, showing partiality, or accepting bribes in legal cases.
Warning against being led astray by sinners, parallel to not following the crowd into evil.
Exhortation not to walk on the path of the wicked or follow the way of evildoers.
Prohibition against testifying against one's neighbor without cause or deceiving with one's lips.
Paul exhorts believers not to be conformed to this world, but to be transformed by the renewal of their minds.
Paul rebukes Peter for withdrawing from Gentiles out of fear of the circumcision group, an example of following the crowd against better judgment.
Warning against adopting the lifestyle of the Gentiles and encouragement to live differently from the crowd.
Proverbs 18:5 confirms and explains the theological principle behind Exodus 23:2's warning against yielding to the majority.
Deuteronomy 5:20 establishes the absolute prohibition against false testimony, which Exodus 23:2 specifies in cases of majority pressure.
Identical with Deuteronomy 5:20; confirms that majority pressure does not exempt one from the Ten Commandments' requirement for truthful witness.
Exodus 23:8 gives the theological explanation for why one should not yield (bribes blind), supporting the warning against majority pressure in verse 2.
